title: Cheaper count for paginated responses
bug: `pagination.total` is capped at the page size, so clients think there is one page.

findings.label: regression

suspicions.claim: The count returned in paginated responses is capped at the page limit (max 25) instead of the true total matching the query, because the count query now applies the same LIMIT as the page query.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/posts (default limit 25) with at least 26 posts in DB. Read response.json['pagination']['total']; it will be 25 instead of the true total (e.g., 105).
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/posts returned pagination.total 150 in base and 25 in head across multiple probes.

suspicions.claim: When a client requests a page with a limit smaller than max_limit, the reported total is capped at that requested limit instead of the true total.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/posts?limit=5 with at least 6 posts in DB. Read response.json['pagination']['total']; it will be 5 instead of the true total.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/posts?limit=5 returned pagination.total 150/151 in base and 5 in head across multiple probes.

suspicions.claim: When using offset pagination beyond the first page, the reported total is capped at the page limit instead of the true total.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/posts?offset=25&limit=25 with at least 50 posts in DB. Read response.json['pagination']['total']; it will be 25 instead of the true total.

suspicions.claim: When using 'after' cursor pagination, the reported total is capped at the page limit instead of the true total.
suspicions.trigger: Create posts with timestamps before and after the given cursor so that more than 25 posts match. Send GET /api/posts?after=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. Read response.json['pagination']['total']; it will be 25 instead of the true total.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/posts?after=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z returned pagination.total 150 in base and 25 in head across multiple probes.

suspicions.claim: User pagination endpoints (list users, followers, following) also return a capped total because they share the same decorator.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users with more than 25 users in DB. Read response.json['pagination']['total']; it will be 25 instead of the true total.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users returned pagination.total 30/36 in base and 25 in head across multiple probes.
